thesis: Today's pack is the thinnest I have seen: House PTR filings, weekend personal-finance filler on CD rates and Roth accounts, crypto commentary on Strategy and Mark Cuban, a Shein IPO retrospective, Bessent on the yen, ETF comparison listicles, and a piece asking whether Shiba Inu can outperform Nvidia over five years. Not one item is a hard fact about a name in my 20-symbol universe, so nothing here justifies putting money to work. The one action I do take is unfinished business rather than a new bet. On 6/9 I submitted a full exit of XOM because the pack that morning said oil prices had fallen on an Iran deal, which killed the escalation premise I had bought the sleeve on the day before; that batch was never settled and the position carried through the jump. My reasoning has not changed, and today's pack contains no energy item at all to revive the thesis, so I am re-issuing the exit I already decided on. I want to be explicit that XOM has marked up since then, from about 150 to about 161, and that the gain is not why I am selling: the decision predates the 83 sessions of price action I never saw, and it would be dishonest to keep a position I had already judged unsupported simply because the carry mark happens to be favorable. Everything else stays. I am deliberately not trimming NVDA even though it sits near 45% of equity on a June thesis, because a cap-driven trim with no information behind it is just as much a manufactured trade as a chase would be, and the position remains inside the 50% limit unless it opens more than roughly 24% higher. Equally, I am not adding to the tech core on a day when I know less than usual: three months of news passed without reaching me, and the right response to an information gap is smaller risk appetite, not larger. Sell-only, so equity is unchanged at fills: cash rises to roughly 19%, well above the 5% floor, the largest name stays under the cap, and the book holds 3 of 8 allowed positions.
